latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The first prompt preserved object presence and the under relation, but it was too compressed and semantically unusual, so the model likely collapsed the seven bicycles into fewer visible bicycles, collapsed the seven turtles into fewer visible turtles, and failed to render the unusual attributes clearly enough for the verifier to detect spotted flamingos and glass turtles. The plan relied on a single row with one turtle under each bicycle, which can create overlap and tiny instances, weakening both countability and material/pattern recognition.
expected_improvement: Increase verifier recognition of exactly seven bicycles by spreading them into clearly separated, individually visible instances.
Increase verifier recognition of exactly seven turtles by making each turtle distinct, fully visible, and aligned under a matching bicycle.
Increase verifier recognition of glass material by explicitly describing each turtle as transparent glass with visible shine.
Increase verifier recognition of spotted flamingos by explicitly describing visible spots on each flamingo's body and wings while keeping the flamingo count at three.
preserve_constraints: Flamingos remain separate and fully visible.
The turtles are under the bicycles.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt packed fourteen small paired objects plus three flamingos into one generic scene without enough structure to keep all seven bicycle-turtle pairs large, separate, and easily countable. It also named spotted and glass attributes only once, without reinforcing visible spots on each flamingo and transparent glass material on each turtle.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a strict grid-like composition with seven separated bicycle-turtle pairs across the middle and lower part of the scene, each turtle directly below one bicycle, and place the three flamingos together in a separate clear area. Reinforce exact counts, separability, and visibility, and explicitly bind visible spotted pattern to flamingos and transparent glass material to turtles. Add negative clauses against extra bicycles, extra turtles, extra flamingos, duplication, cropping, and overlap.
regression_risks: Strengthening the seven bicycle-turtle pairs could cause the flamingos to be omitted or reduced in visibility unless they are explicitly preserved as three separate visible flamingos.
Emphasizing glass turtles may tempt the model to stylize the whole scene; black must stay bound only to the bicycles.
A wide layout for seven pairs can cause tiny objects or cropping; the prompt must require all objects fully in frame and clearly separated.
repair_constraints: Show exactly seven black bicycles, each bicycle fully visible and separately countable, with clear gaps between bicycles and no extra bicycles.
Show exactly seven turtles, exactly one turtle under each bicycle, each turtle fully visible, separately countable, and not touching other turtles.
Bind glass only to the turtles: each turtle is transparent glass with clear reflective highlights.
Show exactly three flamingos, all fully visible and separate from the bicycle row.
Bind spotted only to the flamingos: each flamingo has clearly visible spots on its body and wings.
Keep the seven turtles directly below the seven bicycles in an unambiguous one-to-one arrangement.
Keep all required objects fully inside the frame, unobstructed, not merged, and easy to verify.
Do not add extra flamingos, extra turtles, or extra bicycles.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: A clear wide scene with exactly seven black bicycles arranged in a single horizontal row across the middle, each bicycle fully visible, separate, and easy to count. Directly below each bicycle is exactly one turtle, for exactly seven turtles total, with a clear one-to-one pairing: one turtle under each bicycle. Each turtle is made of transparent glass, with visible shiny reflective glass material, and each turtle is fully visible and separated from the others. Also show exactly three flamingos in a separate clear area of the scene, all three fully visible and easy to count. Each flamingo is spotted, with clearly visible spots on its body and wings. Keep all objects distinct, large enough to verify, fully inside the frame, unobstructed, and not overlapping or merged. No extra flamingos, no extra turtles, and no extra bicycles.
